name_note: GTDB R232 splits classical Streptococcus salivarius into several species; the genomes in s__Streptococcus salivarius_F are labelled Streptococcus salivarius in NCBI, so published work does not separate this lineage.

sentences.text: Streptococcus salivarius has been described as a prominent oral commensal bacterium with probiotic potential and relevance to both oral and systemic health.
A review describes Streptococcus salivarius as a lactic acid bacterium and a well established synthesiser of both broad- and narrow-spectrum antimicrobials.
The oral probiotic strain K12 produces at least three antimicrobials, salivaricin A, salivaricin B and salivabactin, the last controlled by environmental acidification.
A study of pneumonia reported that alterations of the intestinal microbiota during pneumonia featured a reduction in the relative levels of Streptococcus salivarius.
